title: Orsen and the Will
premise: When the coffin of Harrow's End founder Edmund Voss is exhumed for a cemetery relocation, coroner Gideon Amberdale finds it empty—and in its place, a fresh will naming her as executor of an estate she never knew existed. Following the will's cryptic conditions, Gideon uncovers that five townspeople, including her own late mother, helped fake Voss's death thirty years ago to cover a drowning that was no accident. As the surviving conspirators begin dying one by one, Gideon realizes the 'will' was written by someone still alive who wants the truth dragged into daylight before they take the last secret—the identity of the child who survived that night—to their grave. In the end, Gideon discovers she herself is that child; the final conspirator is the town's gentle archivist, who has been killing to protect her from learning what her mother did, and Gideon must choose between exposing the truth and preserving the only belonging she has ever known.
about_author: Ulyana Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former rural registrar who spent a decade cataloguing births and deaths in small-town municipal archives before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about the quiet violence hidden inside close-knit communities, and lives somewhere with too many cemeteries and not enough questions asked.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Oak
chapters.summary: Gideon Amberdale supervises the exhumation of founder Edmund Voss, required for the reservoir expansion, and opens a coffin she expects to be thirty years heavy. It is empty except for a sealed envelope bearing her name. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: the cold shock of a professional certainty shattered—she knows every grave, and this one lied.

chapters.title: A Will Written Yesterday
chapters.summary: The document inside is a will, dated three weeks ago, appointing Gideon executor of the Voss estate on condition she solve 'the matter of 1994' within forty days or the estate passes to the county—with its damning records intact. The lawyer who notarized it has vanished. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: dread braided with reluctant fascination; she cannot walk away.

chapters.title: Five Names in the Margin
chapters.summary: Gideon cross-references the will's odd phrasing against old coroner's logs and finds five names penciled in a margin—all present in town the night Voss allegedly died, including her mother, dead two years now. She interviews the first survivor, retired sheriff Dale Pruitt, whose alibi is rehearsed. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: the vertigo of suspecting the people who raised you.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Dale Pruitt is found drowned in his bathtub, staged to echo the original death. Gideon rules it murder but the acting sheriff wants suicide. Searching Pruitt's house, she finds a photograph of four adults and a child at the riverbank, faces scratched out. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: grief curdling into fear—the will's clock is ticking in blood.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Patience
chapters.summary: Gideon consults Maren Halloway, the town archivist who has catalogued Harrow's End for decades and was her mother's closest friend. Maren offers help but deflects every question about 1994. A second conspirator, councilwoman Ruth Ives, flees town the same night. POV: alternating Gideon and brief Maren passages hinting at protective motives. Emotional beat: warmth with something buried under it.

chapters.title: Alibis Thirty Years Deep
chapters.summary: Reconstructing the night of Voss's disappearance, Gideon learns the five conspired to hide that Voss drowned a man—a drifter no one ever reported—and faked his own death to escape scandal. Her mother forged the death certificate. The empty coffin means someone removed the body recently. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: moral nausea; every institution she trusted was complicit.

chapters.title: Ruth Ives, Returned in Pieces
chapters.summary: Ruth Ives is found alive but beaten, having received the same kind of letter Gideon did—someone is forcing confessions. Ruth names the fifth conspirator: the vanished lawyer, Corwin Ashe. Gideon tracks Ashe's cabin and finds it burned, with signs he left alive. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she is also being herded toward a designed ending.

chapters.title: My Mother's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Forensic comparison reveals the will's handwriting is her mother's—not forged recently, but written before her death and held by someone. Gideon confronts the possibility her mother orchestrated everything posthumously, including Gideon's appointment, to force the truth out. POV: Gideon, intimate and raw. Emotional beat: betrayal and love entangled; the will becomes a message from the dead.

chapters.title: The Last Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Maren lures Gideon to the riverside on the fortieth night and confesses: she removed Voss's body, killed Pruitt, and burned Ashe's cabin—not to protect the conspirators, but to protect Gideon, the child at the riverbank, from learning her mother helped bury a man alive to silence him. Maren offers Gideon the choice: burn the last record or read it. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: climax—identity and belonging balanced on a single page.

chapters.title: Executor
chapters.summary: Gideon reads the record, then makes her ruling as coroner: she files the true cause of death, closes the Voss case publicly as remains unrecoverable, and turns Maren over to the law while keeping her mother's role sealed in her own heart. She buries the empty coffin with a name on the stone—hers, reclaimed. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: costly resolution; belonging chosen knowingly, survival paid for honestly.
